title: The Drowned Salt Anew
premise: Bram Kavanagh, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a smuggler's guide in the Thornfell mountains, takes in a feral child named Wren who speaks the drowned tongue of a kingdom erased from every map. Wren's words begin waking the salt-drowned dead beneath the lowlands, and Bram learns the child is the last vessel of dragon-fire memory, hunted by the Hollow Court—a king whose crown has been worn by something older and hungrier for three hundred years. To save Wren, Bram must return to the capital that exiled her, ally with the very order that branded her traitor, and unbind the king from his parasite before the last dragon-fire gutters out. She succeeds at terrible cost: the king dies free, the drowned kingdom is finally allowed to rest, and Bram—choosing love over the duty she was born to—raises Wren in the mountains, no longer invisible but no longer alone.
about_author: Silas Voss is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing drowned coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about stubborn people, old debts, and the sea's long memory.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram guides a smuggler caravan through a snowbound pass, using her suppressed storm-calling to read weather like scripture. POV: Bram. Beat: weary competence masking loneliness; she has made invisibility an art.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dark
chapters.summary: At her remote waystation, Bram finds a mud-caked girl of eight on her doorstep, speaking a language no living throat should know. POV: Bram. Beat: unease curdling into reluctant protectiveness.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Bram names the child Wren and tries to teach her common speech; Wren instead teaches Bram fragments of the drowned tongue. POV: Bram. Beat: tentative tenderness; two exiles of different kinds.

chapters.title: What the Salt Sings
chapters.summary: Wren sleepwalks to the river and sings; fish rise dead, and the water tastes of brine though the sea is forty miles off. POV: Bram. Beat: dread—the child carries something vast.

chapters.title: The Order's Long Arm
chapters.summary: A traveling relic-hunter recognizes storm-signs around Bram's home and warns that the Vigilant Order still pays for her head. POV: Bram. Beat: paranoia rekindled; her past has teeth.

chapters.title: The Drowned Kingdom of Aelmarrow
chapters.summary: Wren draws maps of a city beneath the sea, matching ruins Bram once saw diving. POV: Bram. Beat: wonder and horror braided together.

chapters.title: Riders on the Low Road
chapters.summary: Hollow Court riders pass through asking after a 'singing child'; Bram lies with a smuggler's fluency. POV: Bram. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve—she will not give Wren up.

chapters.title: Storm-Called
chapters.summary: When riders circle back, Bram breaks her exile's vow and calls a storm to scatter them, revealing herself after ten years of silence. POV: Bram. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt; the sky knows her name again.

chapters.title: The Vigilant Offer
chapters.summary: Order marshal Ilsa Corvane arrives not with chains but a bargain: help us reach the Hollow King, and your exile ends. POV: Bram. Beat: bitter negotiation; duty wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Wren Runs
chapters.summary: Overhearing the bargain, Wren flees into the mountains, and Bram tracks her through a whiteout, nearly losing her to a crevasse. POV: Bram. Beat: terror of loss; love declared plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Crown That Eats
chapters.summary: Corvane explains the truth: the king died generations ago; something ancient wears him like a glove, feeding on dragon-fire memory. POV: Corvane. Beat: cold revelation; the enemy is older than nations.

chapters.title: Down from Thornfell
chapters.summary: Bram, Wren, and Corvane descend toward the lowlands, pursued by Court hunters and haunted by rising tides. POV: Bram. Beat: reluctant alliance; the road narrows.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: At a border river, an old ferryman recognizes Bram's mother's sigil and ferries them free, whispering that her family served Aelmarrow once. POV: Bram. Beat: inheritance surfacing—her blood has older obligations.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wells
chapters.summary: Inland villages find seawater in their wells; Wren's presence wakes the drowned dead, who stand in fields at night, waiting. POV: Wren (rendered through Bram). Beat: guilt—Wren is both key and catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Vigilant Citadel
chapters.summary: The party reaches the Order's citadel; Bram faces the hall where she was branded traitor at nineteen. POV: Bram. Beat: old wounds reopened; judgment remembered in stone.

chapters.title: Archives of Ash
chapters.summary: In forbidden archives, they learn the crown-thing is the Hunger Below, bound by Aelmarrow's last dragons, and only living dragon-fire can renew the binding—or end it. POV: Corvane. Beat: hope with a knife's edge.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Cell
chapters.summary: Order hardliners imprison Bram pending 'trial,' separating her from Wren; Corvane's loyalty fractures under internal politics. POV: Bram. Beat: betrayal within the alliance.

chapters.title: Wren Taken
chapters.summary: Court agents infiltrate the citadel and seize Wren, leaving dead wardens and a single word written in salt: COME. POV: Bram. Beat: despair igniting fury.

chapters.title: Broken Chains
chapters.summary: Corvane frees Bram against orders; together they fight out of the citadel as the Court's riders burn the gates. POV: Bram. Beat: trust forged in fire; enemies become comrades.

chapters.title: The King's Road
chapters.summary: They ride for the capital of Vhalcrest along the old royal road, gathering smuggler allies who owe Bram favors. POV: Bram. Beat: unlikely army assembling; loyalty repaid.

chapters.title: The Drowned Dead March
chapters.summary: The risen dead of Aelmarrow converge on Vhalcrest, drawn by Wren; villages empty ahead of a silent, walking tide. POV: Bram. Beat: apocalyptic awe; history demanding its due.

chapters.title: Gates of Vhalcrest
chapters.summary: Vhalcrest seals its walls against both the dead and the Court; Bram's smugglers get them in through the flooded undercity. POV: Bram. Beat: homecoming to a hostile city; claustrophobic tension.

chapters.title: The Hollow Audience
chapters.summary: Disguised as pilgrims, Bram sees the king enthroned—a man-shaped absence, eyes like tide-pools, Wren caged beside him. POV: Bram. Beat: horror of the hollowed; love tested at distance.

chapters.title: The Man Beneath
chapters.summary: A dying courtier reveals the king's original soul still flickers inside, reachable through memories of his daughter—dead three centuries. POV: Corvane. Beat: fragile hope; the enemy may be saved.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire Guttering
chapters.summary: Wren's flame dims as the Hunger feeds; Bram realizes the binding fails within days, dooming the coast. POV: Bram. Beat: ticking clock made flesh.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' War
chapters.summary: Bram's allies sabotage the Court's fleet in the harbor while Corvane turns half the Order against its corrupt Grandmaster. POV: Bram. Beat: rebellion blooming; ordinary people choosing sides.

chapters.title: Grandmaster's Fall
chapters.summary: Corvane confronts the Grandmaster, who has secretly fed souls to the crown for decades; he dies taking her confession with him. POV: Corvane. Beat: costly victory; grief amid triumph.

chapters.title: Into the Undercity
chapters.summary: Bram dives the flooded vaults beneath the palace where Aelmarrow's last dragon egg sleeps, guarded by her own ancestors' bones. POV: Bram. Beat: inheritance fully revealed—her line were fire-keepers.

chapters.title: The Egg and the Ember
chapters.summary: Bram wakes the dormant egg with her storm-blood, receiving a spark of true dragon-fire—and a vision of Aelmarrow's final night. POV: Bram. Beat: communion with the past; purpose crystallized.

chapters.title: Palace of Tides
chapters.summary: The risen dead breach the palace as the sea itself rises; Bram fights through drowning halls to the throne room. POV: Bram. Beat: chaos climax approaching; everything converges.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Before the throne, Bram begins the rite to separate king from crown while Corvane holds back the Hunger's wraith-servants. POV: Bram. Beat: desperate ritual; love and duty pulling opposite ways.

chapters.title: The King Remembers
chapters.summary: Through Wren's borrowed voice, Bram reaches the buried king with the memory of his daughter; he weeps and turns against the thing that wears him. POV: Bram. Beat: compassion as weapon; the emotional summit.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wants
chapters.summary: The Hunger abandons the dying king and seizes Wren as its new vessel, offering Bram her heart's desire—her exile undone, her family restored—if she kneels. POV: Bram. Beat: temptation at its cruelest.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Bram refuses, choosing the child over every debt of blood and office, and drives the dragon-spark into the crown itself. POV: Bram. Beat: the theme made action; sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Crown and Hunger burn together; the king dies free, whispering thanks; Wren hovers at death's edge with the fire guttering in her chest. POV: Bram. Beat: victory laced with devastation.

chapters.title: Breath of the New Dragon
chapters.summary: The egg Bram woke hatches in the ruined throne room; the hatchling breathes its first fire into Wren, renewing what was lost. POV: Bram. Beat: rebirth; grief answered by wonder.

chapters.title: Let the Dead Sleep
chapters.summary: With the Hunger gone, the drowned dead of Aelmarrow bow to Wren and sink at last into restful salt; the sea recedes. POV: Bram. Beat: mourning transfigured into peace.

chapters.title: Terms of Pardon
chapters.summary: The new regency offers Bram full pardon and a marshal's rank; she declines, asking only freedom and quiet land. POV: Bram. Beat: refusing the crown offered her; duty redefined as choice.

chapters.title: Up the Mountain Again
chapters.summary: Bram, Wren, and the young dragon climb back into Thornfell as spring breaks; Corvane promises letters, not summons. POV: Bram. Beat: bittersweet farewell; found family affirmed.

chapters.title: The Drowned Salt Anew
chapters.summary: A year later, Wren speaks both tongues and teaches Bram songs of Aelmarrow; storms come when called, and go when asked. POV: Bram. Beat: resolution—invisibility traded for belonging; love outlasting duty.
